parsed.explanation: The worst documented features are state-tolerated targeting: routine police detention of trans people on pretexts, on-the-spot extortion, blackmail, demands for sexual favours, and documented rape by state security officers; plus custody harms including court-ordered 'gender determination' and nonconsensual procedures (2025 torture finding). The enforced sexuality statutes (upheld 2019, up to 14–21 years) operate as a police lever against gender-nonconforming people, so they weigh materially, not as dead letter. Societal hostility is documented (pseudonyms needed to move through public space; bathroom fear). Mitigation: courts have repeatedly worked FOR trans people — forced-exam ban with compensation, association rights, the 2025–2026 trans rulings — but Parliament has enacted nothing, remedies are slow, and a death-penalty Family Protection Bill remains pending. No border/facility or violence-rate data; entry treatment is an open question, not an exposure. This sits in high risk, between the police-raid and custody-abuse profiles, lifted slightly by a live, partly protective judiciary.
